# Remote Control Server protocol

<!-- Generated by tools/offline_check/run.sh --update-protocol from the command definitions in
     RegisterCommands (RemoteControlServer.cs) and tools/offline_check/protocol_header.md. Edit those, not this file. -->

## Messages

- One ASCII command per message: the command name, a space, then its arguments, e.g. `SetMagnetDAC 5.1` or `SetDeflection AX,100`.
- Command names are case sensitive.
- Numbers use `.` as the decimal separator.
- Every command gets exactly one reply: a value, `OK`, or a line starting with `Error:`.
- A running server lists its commands with `Help`, and describes one with `Help <command>`.

### Request ids

Any command can start with `#<id> `. The reply then starts with the same id: `#42 GetMagnetDAC` → `#42 5.1`.
If the same client sends the same id and command again within `Config.request_id_window` ms (10 s), it gets the cached
reply and the command is not run again, so retrying a UDP request is safe.

### UDP

Send the command as one datagram; the reply comes back to the sending address and port.

### TCP

By default a connection carries one command: connect, send the command, read the reply until the server closes the
connection. A client that sends nothing is dropped after `Config.tcp_read_timeout` ms (5 s).

If the first command on a connection is

- `KeepAlive` – the server replies `OK` and keeps the connection open. Send newline terminated commands; each reply ends
  with a newline. The connection is closed after `Config.tcp_idle_timeout` ms (60 s) without a command.
- `Subscribe` – the server writes `<scan count>|<data>` and a newline for every scan until the client disconnects.
  `Subscribe` is also allowed after `KeepAlive`.

Commands that only read the server's own state (scan data, `GetMagnetMoving`, `Ping`, `Help`, `GetVersion`) answer at
once. Commands that use the hardware run one at a time.

## Errors

| Reply | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `Error: Invalid Command` | No such command |
| `Error: missing argument for <command>` | |
| `Error: invalid number in <command>` | |
| `Error: could not read <parameter>` | Qtegra could not read the parameter, usually because the name is not in the hardware database |
| `Error: could not set <parameter> to <value>` | |
| `Error: unknown detector <name>` | Not in the detector names configured for the instrument |
| `Error: magnet is moving` | A `SetMagnetDAC` or `SetMass` move is still running |
| `Error: timeout` | `GetNextData` saw no new scan in time |
| `Error: no data` | No scan received yet |
| `Error: <message>` | Anything else; the details are in the Qtegra log |

## Finding parameter names

`GetParameter`, `SetParameter`, `Open`, `Close` and `GetValveState` take the name of an item in the instrument's
hardware database, e.g. `Field Set`, `Y-Symmetry Set`, `CDD Supply Set`, `Deflection AX Set`.

- **Hardware database file**: `C:\ProgramData\Thermo\Qtegra\_Application Data\PluginData\<instrument>\<instrument>.imhwd`
  on the instrument PC. The Hardware Configurator in Qtegra's Configurator tool shows the same items.
  `tools/list_parameters.py` extracts candidate names from that file.
- **Check names against a running server**: `CheckParameters <name>,<name>,...` replies `True` for each name Qtegra can
  read. `python3 tools/smoke_test.py <host> --parameters <file>` checks a whole list.
- **Scripting manual**: the Qtegra Scripting Language Software Manual (P/N 1383460) lists the Helix SFT hardware items
  in chapter 3.
- `ProbeInstrument` logs what the instrument object exposes, to look for a way to list the parameters from the script.

# Commands

## General

| Command | Arguments | Reply | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `GetVersion` |  | `<version>` | Version of this script. |
| `Help` | `[<command>]` | `<command>,<command>,... \| <usage>` | All command names, or the usage of one command. |
| `Ping` |  | `OK` | Check that the server is answering. |
| `KeepAlive` |  | `OK` | TCP only, and only as the first command on a connection: keep the connection open for newline terminated commands and replies. |
| `GetTuningSettingsList` |  | `<name>,<name>,...` | Saved tune settings. |
| `SetTuningSettings` | `<name>` | `OK \| Error` | Load a saved tune setting. |
| `GetIntegrationTime` |  | `<seconds>` | Integration time of the monitor scan. |
| `SetIntegrationTime` | `<seconds>` | `OK \| Error` | Restart the monitor scan with a new integration time. |
| `BlankBeam` | `true \| false` | `OK \| Error` | true remembers Y-Symmetry and sets it to -50, false restores it. Does nothing when Config.use_beam_blank is false. |

## Scan data

| Command | Arguments | Reply | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `GetData` |  | `<name>,<value>,... \| <value>,...` | Latest scan. Name,value pairs when Config.tag_data is true, values only when false. "Error: no data" before the first scan. |
| `GetDataN` |  | `<scan count>\|<data>` | Latest scan with its scan count, which goes up by one for every scan. &lt;data&gt; is as for GetData. |
| `GetNextData` | `[<timeout s>] [<scan count>]` | `<scan count>\|<data> \| Error: timeout` | Wait for a scan newer than &lt;scan count&gt; (default: the latest scan now). Timeout defaults to 5 s. Over UDP this holds up other commands while it waits. |
| `Subscribe` |  | `<scan count>\|<data> per scan` | TCP only: the server writes one line per scan until the client disconnects. Allowed as the first command or after KeepAlive. |
| `ProbeScanData` |  | `OK` | Diagnostic: log the structure of the next scan to the Qtegra log. |

## Cup and sub cup configurations

| Command | Arguments | Reply | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `GetCupConfigurationList` |  | `<name>\r<name>...` | Cup configuration names, separated by carriage returns. |
| `GetSubCupConfigurationList` | `<cup name>` | `<name>\r<name>...` | Sub cup configuration names of a cup configuration. |
| `GetActiveCupConfiguration` |  | `<name>` |  |
| `GetActiveSubCupConfiguration` |  | `<name>` |  |
| `GetSubCupParameters` |  | `<parameter>,<value>;...` | Deflection of each detector of the selected instrument, then CDD Supply Set. Unreadable parameters are left out. |
| `ActivateCupConfiguration` | `<cup name> <sub cup name>` | `OK \| Error` | Names cannot contain spaces. |

## Ion counters (CDD)

| Command | Arguments | Reply | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `ActivateIonCounter` | `<detector>` | `OK \| Error` | Activate and unprotect one CDD, then restart the monitor scan. |
| `DeactivateIonCounter` | `<detector>` | `OK \| Error` | Deactivate and protect one CDD, then restart the monitor scan. |
| `ActivateAllCDDs` |  | `OK \| Error` | Activate and unprotect every CDD with a mass in the active cup configuration. |
| `DeactivateAllCDDs` |  | `OK \| Error` | Deactivate and protect all CDDs. |

## Valves

| Command | Arguments | Reply | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Open` | `<valve>` | `OK \| Error` | Set the valve parameter to 1, e.g. Open Valve Ion Pump Set. |
| `Close` | `<valve>` | `OK \| Error` | Set the valve parameter to 0. |
| `GetValveState` | `<valve>` | `True \| False \| Error` | True when open. |

## Magnet

| Command | Arguments | Reply | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `GetMagnetDAC` |  | `<value>` | Field Set, 0-10 V. |
| `SetMagnetDAC` | `<value>` | `OK \| Error` | Set Field Set, 0-10 V. Moves larger than Config.magnet_move_threshold are stepped in the background: poll GetMagnetMoving. |
| `GetMagnetMoving` |  | `True \| False` | True while a SetMagnetDAC or SetMass move is running. |
| `SetMass` | `<mass>[,<cup>]` | `OK \| Error` | Put &lt;mass&gt; on &lt;cup&gt; (default AX). Deactivates the CDDs first; large moves are stepped. |

## Source

| Command | Arguments | Reply | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `GetHighVoltage` |  | `<V>` | Acceleration Reference Set in V. |
| `SetHighVoltage` | `<V>` | `OK \| Error` |  |
| `GetHV` |  | `<kV>` | Acceleration Reference Set in kV. Note: SetHV takes V. |
| `SetHV` | `<V>` | `OK \| Error` | Same as SetHighVoltage. Note: takes V although GetHV returns kV. |

## Detectors

| Command | Arguments | Reply | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `ProtectDetector` | `<detector>,On \| Off` | `OK` | On saves the deflection and sets it to 2000, Off restores it. |
| `GetDeflection` | `<detector>` | `<value> \| Error` | Deflection &lt;detector&gt; Set. |
| `SetDeflection` | `<detector>,<value>` | `OK \| Error` |  |
| `GetDeflections` | `<detector>[,<detector>...]` | `<value>,<value>,...` | 0 for a deflection that cannot be read. |
| `GetIonCounterVoltage` |  | `<value> \| Error` | CDD Supply Set. |
| `SetIonCounterVoltage` | `<value>` | `OK \| Error` |  |
| `GetGain` | `<detector>` | `<value> \| Error` | Detector gain from the calibration data. |
| `SetGain` | `<detector>,<value>` | `OK \| Error` |  |

## Hardware parameters

| Command | Arguments | Reply | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `GetParameter` | `<parameter>` | `<value> \| Error` | Any item in the instrument's hardware database, e.g. Field Set. See "Finding parameter names". |
| `SetParameter` | `<parameter>,<value>` | `OK \| Error` |  |
| `GetParameters` | `<parameter>[,<parameter>...]` | `<value>,<value>,...` | 0 for a parameter that cannot be read: use CheckParameters to tell. |
| `CheckParameters` | `<parameter>[,<parameter>...]` | `True \| False,...` | True for each parameter that can be read. |
| `ProbeInstrument` |  | `OK` | Diagnostic: log the instrument object's properties and members to the Qtegra log, to look for a list of its parameters. |
